statusText: Roughly 14 minutes after the U.S. cash open (13:30 UTC) and 14 minutes before preliminary UMich sentiment (14:00 UTC), conditions are calm and two-sided. July Retail Sales printed -0.6% MoM, a sharp miss versus +0.1% expected and the steepest drop since May 2025, yet the cash-open reaction was modest and mixed (S&P +0.08%, Dow -0.13%, Nasdaq +0.17%) -- not a persistent one-way reaction. NQ futures have traded a narrow ~110pt (0.36%) range (30,124-30,232) around a flat open, currently near 30,178, roughly mid-range -- no evidence of shallow pullbacks or repeated extension. VIX eased slightly to ~14.52 and 2Y/10Y Treasury yields held near 4.20%/4.68% (Aug 12 benchmark reads, no confirmed fresh print intraday). The Strait of Hormuz blockade remains in force with reported near-zero tanker transits and oil continuing to firm (WTI ~$84.8, Brent ~$93.3, both up from the prior run's $82.1/$87.9 reads) -- a continuation of the standing standoff rather than a new kinetic escalation. Alpha Vantage's TREASURY_YIELD, GLOBAL_QUOTE, WTI and BRENT calls succeeded this run (quota reset), while MARKET_STATUS returned a transient gateway error on both attempts and was not retried further; live retail-sales, VIX, NQ intraday range and geopolitical context came from WebSearch. Confidence is meaningfully higher than the prior run given the confirmed Retail Sales print and successful Alpha Vantage data.
recommendation: Current action remains EA_ON. Tail stays low because NQ itself shows no persistent one-way structure -- the day's only meaningful surprise (the Retail Sales miss) was absorbed with only a modest, mixed cross-index reaction, and futures remain range-bound roughly mid-range between the session high and low. Stress holds moderate into the last scheduled data point of the morning (UMich at 14:00 UTC) and the continuing cross-asset tension from a fully-enforced Hormuz blockade and firming oil; existing-position management and emergency protection remain active through that window regardless of the current EA_ON state. An upgrade to a higher Tail state would require an observed failed-pullback/repeated-extension reaction in NQ itself once UMich has printed and traded, not the pending data point, the standing Hormuz blockade, or oil's continued grind higher on their own.
headline: July Retail Sales printed -0.6% MoM (vs +0.1% expected), the steepest drop since May 2025, but the U.S. cash open absorbed it calmly (S&P +0.08%, Dow -0.13%, Nasdaq +0.17%) with NQ futures range-bound near 30,178 (30,124-30,232 today); VIX eased to ~14.52 and 2Y/10Y yields held near 4.20%/4.68%; the Strait of Hormuz blockade remains fully in force with oil continuing to firm (WTI ~$84.8, Brent ~$93.3); preliminary UMich consumer sentiment (14:00 UTC) is the next checkpoint within the hour.
body: At 13:44 UTC, roughly 14 minutes after the U.S. cash open (9:30am ET / 13:30 UTC), conditions remain calm and largely two-sided. The S&P 500 closed Thursday at a fresh record above 7,800 (7,798.99) on cooler-than-expected inflation data; QQQ closed Thursday at 732.07, +1.16% on the day per Alpha Vantage's latest daily quote. This morning's headline data point, July Retail Sales (Census Advance Monthly), printed a sharp miss: -0.6% MoM versus +0.1% expected, the steepest monthly drop since May 2025, with motor-vehicle sales down 1.8% and nonstore (online) retail down 2.2% MoM; year-over-year growth also decelerated to +5.0% from a revised +7.3% in May. Despite the negative surprise, the cash-open reaction across indices has been modest and mixed rather than persistently directional: the S&P 500 is roughly flat (+0.08%), the Dow is slightly lower (-0.13%), and the Nasdaq is modestly higher (+0.17%). NQ futures opened near 30,201.50 and have traded a narrow range of 30,124.25-30,232.00 (about 110 points, 0.36%) so far today, currently near 30,177.50 -- essentially mid-range, showing no shallow-pullback or repeated-extension structure that would indicate pathological one-way price action. VIX eased slightly to about 14.52 (range 14.48-14.65 today), a calm reading consistent with the muted cash-open reaction. Alpha Vantage's TREASURY_YIELD calls succeeded this run (the daily quota appears to have reset from the prior run's exhaustion): the 2-year Treasury yield stands at 4.20% and the 10-year at 4.68%, both as of the August 12 benchmark read (no fresher intraday print available), essentially unchanged from the prior run's WebSearch-sourced ~4.65% 10-year read. Oil continues to firm on the unresolved Strait of Hormuz standoff: Alpha Vantage's WTI/BRENT daily series show WTI at $84.77 and Brent at $93.26 (as of August 11, the latest available daily print), both up meaningfully from the prior run's ~$82.1/$87.9 WebSearch-sourced reads, consistent with continued tightening. Current reporting describes the blockade as now indefinite with tanker transits through the Strait near zero percent of the pre-war baseline and the IEA warning of rapidly diminishing global oil stockpiles -- an intensified description of the same standing standoff rather than a confirmed new kinetic strike or vessel seizure today, so it is scored as continuation of the existing backdrop, consistent with prior runs, while still acting as a Stress amplifier given the magnitude of the oil move. Preliminary University of Michigan consumer sentiment (10am ET / 14:00 UTC) is the next and final scheduled data point of the morning cluster, landing within the next 15 minutes and layering on top of the already-absorbed Retail Sales miss. Alpha Vantage's MARKET_STATUS call returned a transient Cloudflare gateway error on both the initial attempt and one retry and was not pursued further per the economical-use instruction; this does not materially affect the assessment since the cash-open timing is independently well-established. Tail holds at 8% (low) because no persistent one-way price-path structure -- shallow/no pullbacks, repeated extension after failed retracements, or NQ holding near session extremes -- has been observed in the Nasdaq-100 complex itself; the Retail Sales miss produced only a modest, mixed cross-index reaction, not a directional break. Stress firms to 41% (moderate) reflecting the still-open UMich data point in the next 15 minutes layered on the already-absorbed Retail Sales miss, plus the continued cross-asset tension from a fully-enforced Hormuz blockade and a notable oil move (WTI +$2.7, Brent +$5.3 versus the prior run's reads) against a calm, slightly-lower VIX -- a genuine cross-asset divergence that raises Stress without yet constituting observed Tail structure. Confidence rises to 58% (medium-low), meaningfully above the prior run's 30%, reflecting successful Alpha Vantage yield/oil/equity data (versus the prior run's total outage), a now-confirmed Retail Sales print (versus 'pending' last run), and live VIX/NQ intraday-range confirmation via WebSearch; Confidence is capped below the solid band because the Alpha Vantage yield and oil series are 1-3 days stale (no same-day print) and MARKET_STATUS could not be confirmed.

lookbackSummary: Tail held in the low band (9-16%) through the full prior 24 hours as the index ground to a fresh S&P 500 record above 7,800 on soft CPI/PPI prints; Stress ran elevated to high (up to 51%) around the Wednesday/Thursday CPI-PPI and earnings window before easing into the moderate band (25-33%) through Friday's European morning, then firmed back to 38% heading into today's cash open as the Retail Sales print approached, with no broader transmission confirmed beyond contained single-name after-hours reactions.
outlookSummary: Tail is projected to stay low (3-8%) through the next 24 hours; Stress is projected to peak in the low-to-mid 40s around the 14:00 UTC UMich print before easing steadily through the U.S. afternoon and overnight session into the high-single-digits by Saturday morning UTC, with no forecast slot currently implying an action change from EA_ON. Confidence is projected to decay gradually from the mid-50s toward the mid-30s as the forecast horizon moves away from this run's fresh Alpha Vantage/WebSearch evidence, reflecting normal forecast-horizon uncertainty rather than a new data gap.
